narrative:
The model estimates a 46% chance that you will leave your current role. This is high enough that the organization has decided to deny your promotion, as they are prioritizing employees more likely to stay long-term.

The prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile. Most influential was the fact that you have not received any other job offers while at the company. Employees who do receive outside opportunities are far more likely to stay, so the absence of such offers pushed the model strongly toward expecting you to leave. The second most important factor was your six-to-ten years of experience in this organization. While this is substantial, it is less common among employees the model predicts will remain; most who stay have either much shorter or notably longer tenure here. Finally, your overall career experience of six-to-ten years also contributed, though in the opposite direction. This level of experience is more typical of employees the model believes will stay, giving a modest pull toward retention.

Taken together, the lack of external opportunities and your current tenure created a stronger signal toward departure than your broader experience could offset. The organization should discuss with you ways to increase your sense of future opportunities and stability here. You may wish to explore what additional responsibilities or visibility could strengthen your connection to the role before considering external moves. (218 words)
